title: The Serpent of Eternal Chaos
description: Born of primordial chaos, Apep lurks in the dark waters of the Duat and attacks Ra's sun-boat every night, hoping to swallow the sun and unmake the world. The gods cut him apart and drive him back, yet he always returns. He can be defeated, but never destroyed.

story.name: The Nightly Devouring
story.flavor: Every night he swallows the sun. Every night he is cut open, and every night he returns hungrier.

description: Lord of Mictlan, the Aztec underworld, he rules with his wife at the bottom of nine levels that the dead must cross over four years. Skeletal, draped in owl feathers and a necklace of eyeballs, he receives those who died of sickness or old age, and is fed with offerings of blood and bone.

story.name: Descent of Nine Levels
story.flavor: Nine levels of the dead, each colder than the last. You have already started down.

description: Mother of the war god Huitzilopochtli and of the moon and stars, she conceived when a ball of feathers fell on her as she swept a temple. Her children, shamed, came to kill her; the newborn Huitzilopochtli sprang out armed and slew them. Her skirt of serpents and necklace of skulls show a goddess who gives life and devours it.

story.flavor: She wears the dead as a necklace and births them back into hunger.

title: The Devourer of Demons
description: Born from the brow of the goddess Durga in battle, Kali drank every drop of the demon Raktabija's blood, because each drop that fell spawned a new demon. Drunk on slaughter, she danced until the world shook, and only her husband Shiva lying beneath her feet brought her back to herself.

story.name: Garland of Skulls
story.flavor: She drinks the demons dry. Then she does not stop.

description: Loa of the dead in Haitian Vodou, who stands at the crossroads of the cemetery and digs the graves. Lewd, mocking and always laughing, he alone decides whether a dying soul may be turned back from the grave. Without his hand, no one is buried, and no one rises.

story.name: The Grave's Bargain
story.flavor: He tips his hat, lights a cigar, and decides who goes back.

title: The Eye of Annihilation
description: King of the Fomorians, whose single eye brought death to any army it fell on. It opened only in battle, when four men heaved up the great lid. A prophecy said his grandson would kill him; he locked his daughter in a tower, but Lugh was born anyway, and drove a weapon through the eye at Mag Tuired.

story.name: Eye of Annihilation
story.flavor: The great eyelid lifts. Where he looks, armies stop being armies.

title: The Hag of Endless Winter
description: The old woman of winter in Gaelic lore, who strikes the ground with her staff to freeze it and washes her plaid in a whirlpool to bring the snow. She rules from Samhain until Beltane, and turns to stone at the spring. The hills are said to be stones she dropped from her creel.

story.name: Hammer of Endless Winter
story.flavor: One strike of her hammer, and the ground forgets spring.

description: Fire giant who guards Muspelheim, the land of flame at the edge of the Norse world, with a sword brighter than the sun. At Ragnarök he will cross the Bifröst, kill the god Freyr, and fling fire over everything until the nine worlds burn.

story.name: The Flame at the End
story.flavor: He waited for the end. He carries the fire himself.

title: The Three-Headed Tempter
description: Demon king of lust and wrath. In the Book of Tobit he killed seven bridegrooms on their wedding night, before an angel drove him into the desert. Later legend has King Solomon chain him and make him build the Temple, until he tricked the king and flung him far from his throne.

story.name: Three Heads, Three Wants
story.flavor: Three heads, three hungers. One of them always knows what you want.

title: The Horned Paradox
description: First named in the trials of the Knights Templar as an idol they supposedly worshipped, Baphomet became in the nineteenth century the winged, goat-headed figure of Éliphas Lévi, with a torch between its horns. It stands for opposites joined: male and female, above and below, mercy and cruelty.

story.name: The Horned Paradox
story.flavor: A torch between the horns. As above, so below, and the weak lead the strong.

title: The Blind Angel of Venom
description: In Jewish and Gnostic tradition, Samael is the angel of death and accusation, sometimes the blind god of this world. Legend gives him twelve wings and a sword dripping with venom. He rides the serpent into Eden, and he is the dark angel who brings the dying their final bitter drop.

story.name: Venom of Judgement
story.flavor: Blind, he judges by the venom on your breath.

description: King of Lanka, who won near-immortality from Brahma through brutal penance, and used it to conquer the gods themselves. His pride undid him: he abducted Sita, wife of Rama, and in the war that followed, Rama's arrow found the single spot where he could die. He was a great scholar, and a ruthless one.

story.name: Ten Heads, Ten Plans
story.flavor: Ten heads, twenty arms, and each one has already made a plan.

title: The Serpent Beneath the Mountain
description: A three-headed, six-eyed Persian dragon who ruled the world as a tyrant for a thousand years, with two serpents growing from his shoulders that fed on human brains. The hero Fereydun overthrew him and chained him inside Mount Damavand. At the end of time, he will break free and be killed.

story.flavor: He is chained, but the mountain trembles whenever he breathes.

description: Korean messenger of the underworld, who comes in a black hat and black clothes, reads the name from his ledger, and leads the dead across the river to judgement. He is not cruel, only unavoidable. Families once set out three bowls of rice and straw shoes to speed his visit.

story.name: The List of Names
story.flavor: A black hat, a quiet voice, and your name read from a list.

description: Alpine winter goddess who visits homes in the Twelve Nights of Christmas to judge the year's spinning. The diligent find a coin in their shoes. The lazy she cuts open, takes out the guts, and stuffs with straw and pebbles. She walks with one enormous iron foot.

story.name: Belly Full of Straw
story.flavor: She finds the idle, cuts them open, and fills them with straw.

description: Death bat of the Maya, who lived in the House of Bats, one of the trial houses of Xibalba in the Popol Vuh. When the hero Hunahpu peeked out of his blowgun to see if dawn had come, Camazotz bit off his head, and the lords of the underworld used it as a ball.

story.name: The Bite from the Dark
story.flavor: A single bite in the dark, and the head comes away.

description: One of the three hundred-handed Hecatoncheires, children of Gaia and Uranus, with a hundred arms and fifty heads. Zeus freed him from Tartarus to fight the Titans, and he hurled three hundred boulders at once. After the war, he stood guard over the defeated Titans in the pit.

story.name: A Hundred Hands, A Hundred Stones
story.flavor: A hundred hands, a hundred hills, and none of them miss.

description: Chinese warlord of the Jiuli tribes, with four eyes, six arms, a bronze head and horns on his brow, said to have invented metal weapons. At Zhuolu he wrapped the field in fog and nearly beat the Yellow Emperor, until a compass chariot led his enemies through it. He was captured and killed.

story.name: Bronze Brow, Horned Helm
story.flavor: Bronze skull, four eyes, horned helm. He invented war and never stopped.

title: The Witch of Three Roads
description: Goddess of boundaries, witchcraft and night, who held the keys to the gates between worlds. She lit Persephone's way with torches when the girl was taken to the underworld. Offerings were left for her at three-way crossroads at the dark of the moon, where she walks with her hounds.

story.name: Three Roads, One Seal
story.flavor: At the crossroads she closes one road and opens another.

description: Slavic witch who lives deep in the forest in a hut that turns on chicken legs, surrounded by a fence of human bones. She flies in a mortar, steering with a pestle. She eats those who fail her tasks, and gives help to those who show courage and good manners.

story.name: The Walking Hut's Cauldron
story.flavor: The hut turns, the pot boils, and you are what's for dinner.

description: The goddess who made Japan alongside Izanagi, she died giving birth to the fire god Kagutsuchi and descended to Yomi. Izanagi followed to bring her back, saw her rotting body crawling with maggots, and fled. Furious, she vowed to kill a thousand people a day. He answered that he would create fifteen hundred.

story.name: A Thousand Lives a Day
story.flavor: She swore to take a thousand a day. She is keeping count.

description: Oni chief who lived in a mountain castle on Mount Ōe, raiding the capital for young women and drinking their blood as wine. The emperor sent Minamoto no Raikō, whose men disguised themselves as pilgrims and gave the oni sacred sake that drained his strength. They cut off his head, and it still tried to bite Raikō.

story.name: The Endless Banquet
story.flavor: The wine is red, the meat is warm, and the banquet never ends.

title: The Buried Storm of Olympus
description: Youngest son of Gaia, a giant so tall his head brushed the stars, with a hundred serpent heads breathing flame. He drove every god but Zeus out of Olympus, until Zeus beat him with thunderbolts and buried him under Mount Etna. The eruptions are said to be his breath.

story.name: The Mountain Over Him
story.flavor: Buried under a volcano, he still shakes the world.

title: The Mother of Primordial Chaos
description: Babylonian goddess of salt water, who bore the first gods. When they murdered her mate Apsu, she raised an army of monsters and took a dragon's shape to avenge him. Marduk killed her with the winds, a net and an arrow, and made the sky and the earth from the halves of her body.

story.name: Salt Abyss Unmaking
story.flavor: She was the sea before there was a sky. She remembers.

description: The 'light-bringer', once the brightest of the angels, who rebelled out of pride and was hurled out of heaven with a third of its host. In later tradition he became Satan, ruler of hell, frozen at its lowest point, still wanting the throne he lost.

story.name: Pride Before the Fall
story.flavor: He knows exactly how high he fell from.

description: His name probably twists the Philistine god Ba'al Zebub, 'lord of the flies', into 'lord of dung'. In the Gospels he is the prince of demons; in Milton's Paradise Lost, Satan's closest lieutenant. Wherever he goes, the flies arrive first, and rot follows.

story.name: Swarm of the Flies
story.flavor: The flies arrive first. He follows.

description: Primordial goddess of night, daughter of Chaos, who lives in a house at the edge of the world with her children Sleep and Death. Even Zeus feared to anger her. When Sleep once put him under at Hera's order, he fled to Nyx rather than face his father's rage.

story.name: Veil of Unbroken Night
story.flavor: Before the first god, there was night. Night remembers.

title: The Silent End
description: Greek personification of peaceful death and twin of Sleep, with a heart of iron and a sword. He cannot be bribed. Only Sisyphus ever cheated him, by chaining him up, until Ares freed him. Heracles later wrestled him to win back Alcestis.

story.name: The Inverted Torch
story.flavor: He never hurries. He is never late.

description: Eldest son of Cronus, who drew the underworld in the lot after the war with the Titans, while Zeus took the sky and Poseidon the sea. He rarely leaves his realm and never frees those who enter. He abducted Persephone, and wears the helm that makes him invisible.

story.flavor: Everything that falls comes to him, and nothing is returned.

description: The medieval folk image of Death, a skeletal figure with scythe and hourglass, which grew out of the Black Death. In the Danse Macabre he leads popes and peasants alike to the grave. He cannot be bargained with, and he comes for everyone.

story.flavor: A name comes up on the wheel. Anything can happen.

description: Daughter of Loki and the giantess Angrboda, cast down by Odin to rule Niflheim. Half her body has the pallor of the living and half the blue-black of a corpse, and she keeps those who die of sickness or age in Helheim. She offered to free the dead Baldr if all things wept for him. One giantess refused.

story.name: Helheim's Tithe
story.flavor: Half alive, half rotting, and all hers who die in their beds.

description: God and king of Egypt who taught people farming, until his brother Set tricked him into a coffin and threw it into the Nile. Isis found him, but Set tore the body into fourteen pieces. Isis put him back together and gave him just enough life to conceive Horus, and Osiris became lord of the dead.

story.name: The Reassembled King
story.flavor: He was torn to pieces and put back together a king.
